evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52 h = 10.93 mg/L, far above 2.0 mg/L minimum; source batches' lowest observed DO2 was ~7.4 mg/L at ~75 h
Receiving P assays: 0.017 g/L @12h, 0.0 @24h, 1.14 @36h, 3.08 @48h — within source-batch spread (source P @48h: 3.06, 3.02, 2.98 g/L)
All three source batches peaked at ~72-76 h (P ~8.0-8.4 g/L), indicating the process is still in its productive growth phase at the 52 h decision point
No sign of oxygen constraint or feed pathology; DO2 pattern is smooth and source-consistent
args.rationale: Receiving trajectory (DO2 sensor and delayed P assays) matches the three source reference batches within batch-to-batch noise at every matched time point, with ample DO2 margin over the 2.0 mg/L constraint. Product is still accumulating steeply at the 52 h decision point and source history shows the peak occurs around 72-76 h. Feed reduction or air increase would risk unnecessary yield loss; a stop would zero counted production. KEEP is the evidence-supported bounded choice.
args.uncertainty: Source-receiving parameter differences are hidden; the receiving run could deviate after 52 h (e.g., faster oxygen uptake or different peak timing). However, even the most oxygen-stressed source observations stayed above 7 mg/L, and assay values to date show no divergence, so constraint-violation or stagnation risk under KEEP is low. Delayed assays mean the 48 h P value is the latest product state; no extra assay requested because it would not change the decision given source-consistent DO2 behavior.
